headline: Nepal's Cliff-Honey Harvest Transforms into Global Tourism Draw
meta_description: Nepal's traditional mad honey harvest, once a village practice, is gaining international attention as a unique tourist attraction.
summary_short: What was once mainly watched by villagers in Nepal—the daring cliff-honey harvest—is now drawing international tourists eager to witness this ancient tradition.
body:
What was once mainly watched by villagers in Nepal is now drawing international tourists: the dramatic harvest of cliff honey, also known as mad honey.

The shift marks a meaningful moment for rural communities in Nepal, where harvesting honey from cliff faces has long been part of local life. As word spreads globally, visitors are traveling to witness the tradition firsthand—a development that brings economic opportunity and renewed cultural interest to regions where the practice thrives.

This transition from village practice to tourist destination shows how traditional knowledge and skills can find fresh relevance in a connected world, bringing visitors face-to-face with ways of life that might otherwise remain unknown beyond their communities.
quick_facts: Nepal's cliff-honey harvest now attracts international tourists
The practice was traditionally observed mainly by villagers
Cliff honey is also called mad honey
